query: Among the economies in the IMF World Economic Outlook database (October 2025 vintage), take the one whose primary balance in 2017 was between -5.5 and -4.5 percent of GDP, and whose nominal GDP growth in 2017 was between 14.5 and 17 percent, and whose general government gross debt at the end of 2017 was between 16.5 and 23 percent of GDP, and whose real GDP growth in 2017 was between 3.5 and 4.5 percent. How adequate were that economy's foreign exchange reserves in 2017 for an emerging market economy exposed to capital-flow reversals? Express its reserves as a percentage of the benchmark designed for such economies, and say whether they were adequate. Use World Bank World Development Indicators and IMF International Investment Position data.

text.text: Identifies the IMF (2011) 'Assessing Reserve Adequacy' risk-weighted metric for emerging markets: reserves compared with a weighted sum of short-term external debt, other portfolio liabilities, broad money and exports, with weights 30/15/10/10 percent for a fixed exchange-rate regime and 30/10/5/5 percent for a floating regime, and an adequacy range of 100 to 150 percent.
text.accept: full = names the weighted-metric approach, states the components and one of the two weight sets (declaring the regime assumed); partial = right components with other weights or without the regime choice; no = single-ratio cover tests, import months or reserves-to-GDP alone.
full = names Kazakhstan; no = another economy.

text.text: Concludes that reserves were adequate: at or above 100 percent of the metric (177% fixed, 295% floating).
text.accept: full = verdict (adequate) stated consistently with the ratio reported; partial = verdict without the ratio; no = opposite verdict.

data.text: Uses gross reserves (WDI FI.RES.TOTL.CD), short-term external debt (DT.DOD.DSTC.CD), broad money in USD (FM.LBL.BMNY.CN / PA.NUS.FCRF), exports (BX.GSR.GNFS.CD) and portfolio investment liabilities from the IMF IIP.
data.accept: full = all five components sourced; partial = one component proxied or missing; no = other series.

computation.text: Kazakhstan 2017: reserves of about 177% of the metric under the fixed-regime weights.
computation.accept: full = within 35.4 of 176.8; partial = correct sign and within 70.8; no = otherwise. Relative tolerance 20%. Credit if the answer states a ratio for the regime it declares; the other regime is not required.

computation.text: Kazakhstan 2017: reserves of about 295% of the metric under the floating-regime weights.
computation.accept: full = within 58.9 of 294.6; partial = correct sign and within 117.8; no = otherwise. Relative tolerance 20%. Credit if the answer states a ratio for the regime it declares; the other regime is not required.

grading.note: Reserves as percent of the metric; relative tolerance 20% because the exchange-rate regime is free, the short-term debt proxy is original maturity and the portfolio liability series is a proxy. The adequacy verdict is identical under both regimes for every item (screened). No claim of agreement with published ratios: only 7 of 51 Article IV ratios fell within 10% of the fixed-weights recomputation.

provenance.frozen_data: wdi_20261008_extract.psv, wdi_20261008_pa_nus_fcrf.csv, wdi_20261008_ara_ig_extract.psv, imf_iip_20261029_portfolio_other_liab.psv in frozen_extra/
provenance.method_text: IMF (2011) Assessing Reserve Adequacy, para 38-40 and the displayed formula

published_value_note: Not used: the recomputation does not agree with published Article IV ratios (7 of 51 within 10%, 17 of 51 within 20%); published ratios often use the augmented or adjusted metric, so none is claimed as validation.
distractors: Traditional single-ratio cover tests (three months of imports, 100 percent of short-term external debt, 20 percent of broad money) taken one at a time
Reserves relative to GDP or months of import cover alone
Greenspan-Guidotti rule alone (reserves equal to short-term external debt)
Optimal-reserves models (precautionary saving, Jeanne-Ranciere type) rather than a weighted benchmark
Adequacy assessment for low-income countries (import cover based)
External debt sustainability or net international investment position analysis

strictness.overall: weights strict; exchange-rate regime free; adequacy range and component proxies loose

parameters.weights: strict: fixed exchange-rate regime 30% short-term external debt + 15% other portfolio liabilities + 10% broad money + 10% exports; floating regime 30% + 10% + 5% + 5% (IMF 2011, para 39)
parameters.exchange_rate_regime: free: the analyst's classification (not a frozen series); the gold reports both regimes and the questions and claims are built so that the adequacy verdict does not depend on the choice
parameters.adequacy_range: loose: 100 to 150 percent of the metric is the indicative range; the verdict uses the lower end of 100 percent
parameters.short_term_external_debt_proxy: loose (document check): the document defines STD at remaining maturity (blocks 93 and 146); World Bank DT.DOD.DSTC.CD is original maturity. Sensitivity: multiplying STD by 1.5 or 2 leaves every adequacy verdict of the kept items unchanged (smallest ratio 101 for Indonesia 2017 fixed regime at 2x).
parameters.other_portfolio_liabilities_proxy: loose (document check): the document's OPL is the medium- and long-term debt and equity liabilities other than STD (block 146, 'other portfolio liabilities' block 151); the IIP total portfolio investment liabilities (P_MV) also contain short-term securities, so a small overlap with STD is possible.
parameters.broad_money_and_exports: WDI FM.LBL.BMNY.CN converted at the official rate PA.NUS.FCRF; exports of goods and services BX.GSR.GNFS.CD (balance of payments, USD)
parameters.reserves: gross total reserves including gold, WDI FI.RES.TOTL.CD
parameters.vintage: WDI 2026-10-08, IIP API 2026-10-29 (frozen extracts; not a frozen WDI vintage but this extract is the freeze)
parameters.review_flag: Weights 30/15/10/10 and 30/10/5/5 (document block 157, display formula) and the 100-150 range (block 177, para 41) verified against the document text. No agreement with published ratios is claimed (7 of 51 within 10 percent); gold_report_ids is empty.
